overall: The AG found a violation: the chair announced the recording about 14 minutes late, and a wall sign and meeting notice did not satisfy the start-of-meeting requirement. The violation was deemed technical; the Board was ordered to comply going forward.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the chair failed to announce at the start of the January 2 meeting that it was being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, the Law requires that the Chair notify attendees of recordings “[a]t the beginning of the meeting,” and therefore we are constrained to find a violation of the Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with G.L. c. 30A, § 20(f): the chair must inform attendees of any recordings at the beginning of each meeting.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance, and caution that future similar violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
